subject: Shared construction and focused behavioral execution for front-end development
claim: The Windows development checkpoint executed all 329 claims in 29,941 ms with exact project/package cache hits, compared with 225,713 ms while creating those products. A deliberately changed compiler parser invalidated its product key, rebuilt, and returned the required failing owner status in 14,634 ms. Restoring the original source reused its original product and executed the selected 254 claims successfully in 2,101 ms. No compiler semantics were retained from the mutation probes.

limitations: These are single Windows development observations, not stable performance thresholds, clean-machine timings, or paired-host qualification. Existing admitted native tool artifacts were used.
The no-argument 492-case qualification owner was not run. The checkpoint does not qualify candidate WVB 1.39, Foundation payload borrowing, or omitted compiler/runtime phases.

The first source-mutation probe exposed lost child rejection in the new Windows dispatch. That failed attempt is not passing evidence; dispatch was repaired and the retained wrapper regression plus a distinct changed-source probe passed afterward.
Cache-creation cost is still material: the generic-call native package alone took 115,423 ms. Warm full-checkpoint execution is dominated by the roughly 20-second generic type-catalog behavior.

The independent descriptor constructions remain uncached. Compiler-scale reproducibility, fresh qualification, platform boundaries, and malformed-input ownership are not replaced by these development results.
Peak working-set memory was not measured. The new runner enforces a ten-minute deadline, bounded diagnostics and file reads, six products, and bounded termination cleanup.
